idea.idea: Why 80% of businesses see zero financial payoff from AI (and what the profitable 20% do differently)
idea.angle: Paying for generic ChatGPT subscriptions yields zero ROI unless paired with a deterministic automation trigger like invoice extraction or payment reminders.
idea.audience_problem: Small business owners spending monthly fees on AI chat tools without seeing any measurable revenue growth or cost savings.

hooks: Why your AI subscriptions aren't increasing your shop's profit.

slides.title: Before You Renew AI Tools
slides.subtitle: Check these four areas first
slides.body: Does your current AI tool help with these specific business drivers?
items: Does it automate a specific, repetitive task?
Does it save actual labour hours every week?
Is the data output directly actionable for billing?
Are you measuring the time saved vs cost?

slides.title: The Bottom Line
slides.subtitle: How to make AI work for you
items: Stop treating AI as a magic solution.
Use AI only for simple, repetitive calculations.
Rely on your human judgment for client trust.
If it does not show a clear ROI, cancel.

piece.caption: Spending monthly on AI chatbots for your shop? If you aren't seeing a dip in costs or a jump in revenue, you are likely just burning cash. Data shows that for most non-tech businesses, AI is currently a calculator that does not understand trust, ethics, or the specific trade-offs of running a physical business. Don't fall for the hype of 'intelligence'. If your current tool isn't saving you hours on specific tasks like data entry or invoice sorting, it is time to audit your subscriptions. What is one task you tried to automate that failed because it needed a 'human touch' instead?

AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch).
Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity.
“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said.
Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.”
“AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.”
Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains .
